chunks: Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad ibn Qulawayh, from Sa'd ibn Abdallah, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Abdallah ibn Muhammad al-Hajjal, from Yunus ibn Ya'qub who said:

We were at the place of Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) when he (peace be upon him) said: Do you not have a secure shelter? Do you not have a comforter that you can seek comfort in? What prevents you from [referring to] al-Harith bin al-Mughira al-Nasri.

key_terms.الْحَارِثُ بْنُ الْمُغِيرَةِ النَّصْرِيُ: al-Harith bin al-Mughira al-Nasri, a companion
key_terms.مُسْتَرِيح: a source of comfort or rest
key_terms.مُفْزَع: a place of refuge or security

ai.seo_question: Who is al-Harith bin al-Mughira al-Nasri and why did the Imam recommend him as a refuge?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Rijal al-Kashi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) highlights al-Harith bin al-Mughira al-Nasri as a trusted companion and a 'refuge' (muf'azz) for the Shia community, emphasizing his reliability in transmitting hadith. This reference underscores the early Shia practice of relying on specific, verified narrators during periods of political instability, establishing al-Harith as a key figure in the chain of transmission.

en.ammaar-muslim: 1. [1/140] Rijal al-Kashshi: Muhammad b. Qulawayh from Sa`d b. Abdallah from Ahmad b. Muhammad b. Isa from Abdallah b. Muhammad al-Hajjal from Yunus b. Ya`qub who said:

we were at Aba Abdillah عليه السلام’s place when he عليه السلام said: do you not have a secure shelter? do you not have a comforter that you can seek comfort in? what prevents you from [referring to] al-Harith bin al-Mughira al-Nasri.
